title: Consumption-aligned private deployment pilot with dual SLA paths
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Run a structured pricing and packaging experiment for Private/VPC on-premise deployments that pairs a modest fixed license floor with consumption-aligned metering and provides two clearly defined SLA/support paths (Gold: 99.95% + 24x7 ops; Silver: 99.9% + business-hours). The pilot should validate willingness-to-pay, upgrade cadence preferences, and operational load under the two SLA tiers.
hypothesis: Offering a lower entry license with an incremental consumption band will increase conversion in proof-of-concepts while maintaining or improving ARR per account when paired with a higher-cost Gold SLA option for enterprise customers.
pricing_model: Proposed: baseline license fee (annual, covers entitlement + packaged images) + metered GPU-hour consumption for inference. Two SKU modifiers: Gold SLA surcharge (premium percent on license and consumption) and Ops Credits bucket for emergency patches. Optional add-ons: extended retention for observability and accelerated security patch windows.
support_model: Gold SLA: 24x7 on-call + guaranteed 1-hour response for Sev1, quarterly security patch windows with optional hotfix purchase. Silver SLA: business-hours support, standard monthly maintenance windows, 7x24 read-only monitoring access. Clear playbooks for fallbacks between tiers (automatic downgrade to Silver in case of capacity constraints for non-critical workloads).
upgrade_cadence: Baseline release cadence: quarterly feature releases for private deployments with an opt-in accelerated channel for Gold customers (monthly security patches + critical hotfix capability). For air-gapped customers, provide pinned image bundles with serviceable patch windows on request.
acceptance_criteria: 1) At least 6 pilot customers activated across both SLA tiers. 2) >=70% of pilots confirm license+consumption model is easier to budget vs legacy seat or fixed-only pricing. 3) Internal SRE churn measured: no more than 15% increase for Gold trials vs existing Dedicated baseline. 4) Legal/Security sign-off on standard SQ templates and image distribution process.
metrics: ARR_projection: projected ARR per pilot at 12 months
conversion_rate: fraction of pilots converting to paid contract within 90 days
support_load: incoming Sev1/Sev2 events per pilot per month
upgrade_adoption: percent opting into accelerated monthly security channel

decisions: Adopt hybrid pricing: modest annual license floor + consumption metering (GPU-hour) to reduce trial friction.
Two SLA paths (Gold/Silver) to separate predictability vs price-sensitive use cases.
Offer Ops Credits as an explicit add-on for expedited hotfixes rather than burying fee in standard contracts.
tradeoffs: Predictability vs flexibility: license floor improves revenue predictability but may deter very small POCs; consumption alignment lowers barrier but adds billing complexity.
Operational burden: Gold SLA increases SRE on-call demand; mitigations include priced Ops Credits and runbooks for automated failover.
Revenue recognition: combined license+consumption complicates accounting; finance requested explicit examples for ASC 606 treatment.
risks: Customers interpret consumption billing as unpredictable cost—requires clear metering dashboard and spend alerts.
Air-gapped customers may delay upgrades, increasing security risk; need contractual commitments and priced accelerated patching option.
SRE headcount may not scale for multiple Gold pilots simultaneously—hire/contract plan needed if pilots exceed expected support load.
mitigations: Build a simple forecast UI in Console for private deployments showing projected monthly spend and burn rates.
Include explicit SLA onboarding checklist in Solutions Engineering handoff to ensure customers understand upgrade cadence and emergency path.
Limit pilot cohort concurrency to 6 active customers until runbook automation reduces manual toil by 40%.
